The 2025 Arizona Cardinals finished 3-14 over 17 games, scoring 355 points and allowing 488 for a point differential of −133. The offense ranked 23rd in EPA per play at −0.02, and the defense ranked 27th at +0.09. The team averaged 20.9 points per game (23rd of 32) and allowed 28.7 (29th of 32). Final full-season DVOA was −18.5% overall (27th of 32), −6.7% on offense (24th), +4.7% on defense (21st, where lower is better) and −7.1% on special teams (30th).

Jacoby Brissett threw for 3366 yards with 23 TD and 8 INT over 485 attempts, posting an NGS CPOE of +3.5 (7th of 42), though his EPA per dropback was +0.00 (34th of 57). Kyler Murray threw for 962 yards and 6 TD on 161 attempts. Trey McBride was the top target with 169 targets, 1239 yards and 11 TD at +0.43 EPA per target, and Michael Wilson had 126 targets and 1006 yards. The offensive line allowed a 25% pressure rate (26th of 32) and an 8% sack rate (25th). Arizona's PROE of +8.0 was the most pass-heavy in the league (1st of 32).

Josh Sweat led the defense with 12 sacks, 28 pressures and 17 QB hits, and Calais Campbell added 6.5 sacks and 18 pressures. Denzel Burke allowed a 70.8 rating on 54 targets, but Will Johnson allowed 109.1 and the team passer rating allowed was 101.5 (25th of 32). The cornerback group allowed 106.4 (28th) and the Edge/DL group 118.8 (29th). On special teams, Chad Ryland made 25 of 33 field goals.

The 2025 Falcons went 8-9 with a point differential of −48 (353 points scored, 401 allowed). The offense ranked 24th in EPA per play, while the defense ranked 15th in EPA per play allowed, but the pass rush was the standout: 57 sacks and a 9% sack rate (4th highest). Final full-season DVOA (the sheet's latest FTN table) put Atlanta 19th overall (−6.4%), 20th on offense (−2.8%), 12th on defense (−2.7%, where lower is better) and 29th on special teams (−6.3%).

Michael Penix Jr. (9 touchdowns, 3 interceptions, EPA per dropback +0.03 over 302 dropbacks) and Kirk Cousins (NGS CPOE −1.7, 27th of 42; EPA per dropback −0.02, 36th of 57) split the passing. Under-center play action was the best weapon (10% of dropbacks, +0.33 EPA, 4th). Bijan Robinson ran for 1478 yards at 5.1 per carry and was the most efficient target (+0.26 EPA on 103 targets). Kyle Pitts (118 targets) and Drake London (112 targets, 919 yards) led the receivers. The line allowed a 19% pressure rate (11th) and a 4% sack rate (5th).

The pass rush produced the sacks, led by James Pearce (10.5 sacks, 16 QB hits, 27 pressures) and Brandon Dorlus (8.5 sacks). The secondary was mixed: the safety group ranked 6th in rating allowed (83.4), with Xavier Watts and Jessie Bates III combining for eight interceptions, but the cornerbacks ranked 21st (94.4), and Mike Hughes allowed five touchdowns. Special teams were a clear weakness at −6.3% DVOA (29th), with three kickers used and Younghoe Koo making 2 of 3 field goals.

The 2025 Ravens went 8-9 with a +26 point differential (424 points scored, 398 allowed), averaging 24.9 points per game (11th) and allowing 23.4 (18th). The offense ranked 11th in EPA per play (+0.03) and the defense 21st (+0.03, 1 = lowest allowed). The final full-season DVOA of +7.3% (14th) came from an offense at +6.4% (11th), a defense at +1.2% (17th) and special teams at +2.0% (12th). It was a run-first team (PROE −11.2, 31st).

Lamar Jackson threw for 2549 yards, 21 TD and 7 INT (103.8 rating) with +0.06 EPA per dropback (23rd), but his NGS CPOE (−2.6, 33rd of 42) and 3.02-second time to throw (38th of 42) were weak. Derrick Henry ran 307 times for 1595 yards at 5.2 per carry with a +1.05 RYOE (3rd). Zay Flowers was the most efficient target (+0.39 EPA per target on 118), while Mark Andrews (70 targets) managed +0.02. Play action from under center produced +0.29 EPA (10th) and a 61% success rate (2nd). The line allowed pressure on 22% of dropbacks (19th).

Travis Jones led the team with 5 sacks, Tavius Robinson added 4.5 and Mike Green 3.5, but the team produced only 30 sacks. The cornerback group allowed an 85.7 rating (9th), and Nate Wiggins allowed 77.5 on 105 targets, but deep passes were a problem (+0.69 EPA allowed, 25th) and the safety group allowed a 106.9 rating (23rd). Special teams were above average at +2.0% DVOA (12th), with Tyler Loop going 30 of 34 on field goals.

Buffalo finished 12-5 with a +116 point differential (481 points for, 365 against). The offense ranked 3rd in EPA per play (+0.14) and was tied for 4th in points per game (28.3), while the defense ranked 13th in EPA per play allowed (−0.01) and 12th in points allowed per game (21.5). Final DVOA placed the Bills 8th overall (+12.5%), 4th on offense (+15.0%), 20th on defense (+3.2%, lower is better) and 15th on special teams (+0.7%).

Josh Allen posted 3668 yards, 25 TD and 10 INT, with +0.17 EPA per dropback (7th of 57) and +0.44 EPA per carry, despite a 40% pressure-to-sack rate (15th highest of 60) and a time to throw ranked 31st of 42. The line allowed pressure on just 17% of dropbacks (3rd of 32). James Cook was the engine with 309 carries for 1621 yards (5.2 YPC, +1.14 RYOE, 2nd of 51). Dalton Kincaid was the most efficient receiver with 15-plus targets (49 targets, 571 yards, 5 TD, +0.80 EPA per target).

Gregory Rousseau led the defense with 7 sacks, 23 QB hits and 29 pressures, and Joey Bosa added 5 sacks. The team totaled 36 sacks at a 7% rate (14th). The pass defense was solid (−0.07 EPA per dropback, 8th), but the run defense ranked 30th in EPA per rush allowed (+0.05). Cole Bishop allowed a 65.6 rating with 3 INT, and the safeties ranked 8th (84.1). Special teams ranked 15th in DVOA, with Ray Davis returning 31 kickoffs for 943 yards.

The 2025 Panthers went 8-9 with a point differential of −69 (311 points scored, 380 allowed). The offense ranked 26th in EPA per play and the defense 23rd in EPA per play allowed. Final full-season DVOA (the sheet's latest FTN table) put Carolina 25th overall (−13.4%), 25th on offense (−7.9%), 22nd on defense (+5.1%, where lower is better) and 22nd on special teams (−0.5%).

Bryce Young had NGS CPOE −0.3 (21st of 42) and EPA per dropback of −0.01 (35th of 57), with 23 touchdowns and 11 interceptions. The line allowed a 24% pressure rate (24th), and third downs were a problem at −0.27 EPA (27th).

The defense generated little pressure: 30 sacks (a 5% sack rate) and 5.8 pressures per game, the second fewest in the league (31st of 32, where 1 = most). Derrick Brown and Nic Scourton each had five sacks, and Tre'von Moehrig added three with 14 tackles for loss. The cornerbacks were a bright spot, ranked 7th in rating allowed (82.9), with Michael Jackson (four interceptions) and Jaycee Horn (five) leading. Special teams ranked 22nd at −0.5% DVOA.

The 2025 Chicago Bears went 11-6 with a point differential of +26, scoring 441 points (25.9 per game, 9th of 32) but allowing 415 (24.4 per game, 23rd of 32). The offense ranked 8th of 32 in EPA per play (+0.08) and the defense 17th of 32 in EPA per play allowed (+0.02, where lower is better). The line rarely gave up sacks, with a 4% sack rate (3rd of 32), though it allowed a 24% pressure rate (23rd of 32). D'Andre Swift ran 223 times for 1087 yards at 4.9 per carry, and Colston Loveland was the standout target at +0.58 EPA per target on 82 targets. The heavy-set offense was the strength, ranking 1st of 32 in EPA (+0.22).

The team totaled 35 sacks (6% sack rate, 21st of 32) and 7.8 pressures per game (21st of 32). The coverage was the weak point: the cornerbacks ranked 18th of 32 in rating allowed (92.8), the safeties 20th (106.1), and Kevin Byard allowed seven touchdowns. Special teams were average, with Devin Duvernay averaging 26.7 yards on 40 kick returns.

The offense was mid-table (EPA per play −0.01, 20th; offense DVOA +4.4%, 13th), but the defense was the story: it ranked 29th in EPA per play allowed (+0.13) and 30th in DVOA (+16.3%). The final full-season DVOA of −8.6% (21st) was propped up by special teams (+3.3%, 6th).

Motion hurt the passing game: pass EPA was −0.14 with motion (29th) and +0.10 without (7th).

The secondary was the weakest unit: opponents posted a 105.2 passer rating (27th), with linebackers at 115.4 (31st). DJ Turner allowed an 80.5 rating on 68 targets, while Cam Taylor-Britt allowed 130.9 with 4 TD. Special teams were strong, with Charlie Jones returning 42 kicks for 1084 yards.

The 2025 Browns finished 5-12 with a −100 point differential (279 points scored, 379 allowed), scoring 16.4 points per game (31st). The offense was one of the league's worst: 31st in EPA per play (−0.19) and 32nd in offense DVOA (−34.0%). The defense was the better half, ranking fifth in EPA per play allowed (−0.09) and eighth in DVOA (−9.7%), but the final full-season DVOA was −32.7% (31st) with special teams last at −8.4%.

Harold Fannin Jr. led the targets (107, 731 yards, 6 TD) at +0.01 EPA. The line allowed pressure on 30% of dropbacks (32nd), the worst rate in the league.

Myles Garrett had 23 sacks, 39 QB hits, 53 pressures and 33 TFL, with Maliek Collins (6.5 sacks) and Alex Wright (5.5) the other pass rushers, for 53 team sacks (9%, 2nd). The pass defense was uneven: passer rating allowed was 94.9 (15th), with the safeties at 83.6 (7th), but the cornerback group allowed 104.1 (27th) and Myles Harden allowed five TD. Special teams were the league's worst at −8.4% DVOA (32nd), with Andre Szmyt making 24 of 27 field goals.

Courtland Sutton posted an EPA per target of +0.37 on 124 targets, Denver allowed a 3% sack rate, 1st of 32, and a 19% pressure rate, 7th. Special teams were a weakness, with 23 accepted penalties for 190 yards, 24th of 32, and Harrison Butker made 33 of 38 field goals.
